input: Get a comprehensive eye exam and new prescription

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they already have an eye doctor or need to find one entirely changes the first steps of the plan.

A basic refractive exam differs significantly from a comprehensive medical eye exam that checks for conditions like glaucoma or macular degeneration — this determines what type of appointment to book.
The exam may be for the user alone or also for family members, which affects scheduling complexity and provider selection.
Whether they have vision insurance — and which plan — directly determines which providers are in-network and what the out-of-pocket cost will be.
Their location and preferred appointment timeframe determine which providers are reachable and how urgently the plan needs to move.
Whether they want glasses, contacts, or both affects which tests the doctor needs to run and what the prescription outcome should include.
Knowing whether the prescription is just for record-keeping or immediately needed for ordering new eyewear sets the urgency and the definition of 'done.'

gold.taskTitle: Get a comprehensive eye exam and new prescription
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to schedule and complete a full eye exam to obtain an updated vision prescription.

questions.title: Do you have an existing eye doctor to return to?
questions.description: Determines whether the first step is booking with a known provider or researching and selecting a new one.

questions.title: Do you need a full medical eye exam or just a vision check?
questions.description: Distinguishes between a comprehensive ophthalmological exam (checking eye health) and a standard optometry refraction for a glasses/contacts prescription.

questions.title: Is this exam just for you or for others too?
questions.description: Identifies whether family members are also being scheduled, which affects provider selection and appointment logistics.

questions.title: Do you have vision insurance coverage to use?
questions.description: Determines whether in-network filtering is needed and what cost constraints apply when choosing a provider.

questions.title: What city or area are you looking for providers in?
questions.description: Establishes the geographic scope for finding and recommending nearby eye care providers.

questions.title: Will the prescription be for glasses, contacts, or both?
questions.description: Affects which tests the doctor needs to perform during the exam and what the final prescription document should cover.

questions.title: Do you need the prescription urgently to order new eyewear?
questions.description: Sets the timeline and urgency of the plan — whether this is time-sensitive or can be scheduled at leisure.
